ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: “Meet a patriarch, kill the patriarch” belongs to Linji’s enumerated formula of killing whatever is encountered, and later masters quote that wording as a sharp inherited command.
EvidenceBody: Literally, "meet a patriarch, kill the patriarch" . Linji's surviving record places it inside a five-member roster: "meet buddha, kill buddha; meet a patriarch, kill the patriarch; meet an arhat, kill the arhat; meet parents, kill parents; meet kin, kill kin" . This is the Chan bend: the honored religious and familial titles become the grammatical objects of the same repeated verb, and later masters preserve, question, and redeploy that severe roster. A successor record explicitly asks why a good teacher would want to kill people after quoting the three religious members, without supplying a prose gloss. Later uses attach the phrase to a sharp sword, place it opposite "carry the infant and encourage the child" in a contrast about grandmotherly kindness, or quote it in a New Year's address before comments on lineage descent. The records use killing language literally in the formula but do not record bodily killings in these deployments; this entry adds no symbolic object behind the named roster.
